import { build } from 'esbuild';
import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';
const file = process.argv[2] ?? 'src/module.ts';
const r = await build({ entryPoints: [file], bundle: true, minify: true, treeShaking: true,
  format: 'esm', platform: 'browser', target: 'es2022', write: false, metafile: true, logLevel: 'silent' });
const own = Object.entries(Object.values(r.metafile.outputs)[0].inputs)
  .filter(([path]) => !path.includes('node_modules/'))
  .reduce((sum, [, info]) => sum + info.bytesInOutput, 0);
console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks cleanly under `tsc --strict`. I didn't run any input comparisons against the original. The original `src/module.ts` can't be built here because `lodash` isn't installed, so I also have no before/after size comparison.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 606 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of my own code.

The exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged. Each lodash call is replaced by an es-toolkit call:
- **`byId`** uses `keyBy` from `es-toolkit` with the same `(row) => row.id` callback.
- **`totalAge`** uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`. I changed the `'age'` string shorthand to `(row) => row.age`, because the main `sumBy` only takes a function.
- **`isBlank`** uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main `es-toolkit` package has no `isEmpty`. Its `isEmptyObject` would give different results for strings and arrays, so I used the compat version, which follows lodash's behaviour. It adds some bundle size, but no other es-toolkit function keeps the behaviour across the whole input range.

There are no adapters and no lodash imports left.
